title: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

relationships.phenotype: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene, which encodes alpha-II spectrin.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families via next-generation sequencing.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous SPTAN1 mutations in families with dominant hereditary motor neuropathy; 'HMND11' is OMIM's name for the disorder.

checks.claim: The SPTAN1 gene encodes alpha-II spectrin.
checks.evidence_quote: heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1
checks.explanation: The abstract identifies SPTAN1 as the alpha-II spectrin gene.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is a rare inherited peripheral neuropathy with juvenile onset. It is marked by length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons without significant involvement of sensory neurons. Penetrance is variable and severity differs greatly between patients (Beijer et al., 2019).

paragraphs.text: In affected members of 3 unrelated families with autosomal dominant juvenile-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy, Beijer et al. (2019) used next-generation sequencing to identify heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene. In patient cells, the mutant mRNA was degraded by nonsense-mediated decay, which reduced protein levels. Beijer et al. (2019) noted that dominant-negative SPTAN1 mutations had already been described as the cause of a range of epilepsy phenotypes.
